_comment: THE FILES LISTED HERE ARE KOTVA'S, NOT PIER'S. DO NOT EDIT THEM IN THIS REPO.
They are the substrate protocol modules of the `kotva-client` package, carved out
of this SDK because chunkProof.js was a second implementation of a kotva spec
section (substrate/FEEDS.md 5.3) living in a product. Their source of truth is
kotva/bindings/js/src; scripts/check-kotva-parity.mjs fails the test run if a
byte here drifts from the hash recorded for it below.
A fix belongs UPSTREAM: change it in kotva, cut a new bindings/js tag, then run
`npm run kotva:pin -- ../../kotva` to re-sync and re-pin. Editing the copy here
is the exact drift this pin exists to prevent.
PROVENANCE. All eight files are now synced UNIFORMLY from kotva `main` @
db96b9f8f05f3e932bbbc60b627d3d5dfa563312 ("bindings/js: add invalid-signature
+ exact-replay regression tests"), the tip of a four-commit run
(091848c..db96b9f) that widened the core signaling protocol surface for real
consumers. `commit` below is that SHA, recorded in place of `tag`/`version`
because no new bindings/js/vX tag has been cut past bindings/js/v0.1.0 for it
-- `version` still reads kotva-client's unbumped package.json 0.1.0, which is
therefore NOT a precise pointer to this sync; treat `commit` as authoritative.
kotva `main` was verified clean and 104/104 tests green at this commit before
syncing. Previously (as of the ts-migration-2 branch) six of these eight had
been advanced ahead of signaling.js/rendezvousSignaling.js, which stayed JS
pinned to bindings/js/v0.1.0 -- see below for why, and why that no longer
applies. This re-pin folded that split away: re-running `kotva:pin` against
the same checkout picked up two incidental drifts in the previously-advanced
set too (chunkProof.ts: a `let`-destructuring reassignment rewritten to fresh
`const`s, same values, ties into the file's own prefer-const lint history;
rendezvous.ts: `Promise<any>` narrowed to `Promise<unknown>` in three spots
with explicit casts at the JSON-parse boundary) -- both read and confirmed as
type-safety refactors, not protocol changes, before accepting them.
WHY signaling.js / rendezvousSignaling.js were PREVIOUSLY NOT advanced, and
why that is now resolved: kotva's signaling.ts used to type
`SignalPayload.type` as the closed union 'offer'|'answer'|'ice'|'join'|'leave'
and `signal()`'s `toId` as `string` (no null), and defined no `data`/`identity`
fields on SignalPayload, and named the prekey-claim shape `SignedPreKeyClaim`.
pier's own call/fabricSignaling.ts (a real, already-TypeScript consumer, not
test code) sends arbitrary app-level kinds ('join', 'sdp', 'screen-share', ...),
passes `toId: null` for broadcast, and threads `data`/`identity` through the
same envelope -- and pier's own fabric.ts imported the type under the name
`SignedPreKeyAnnouncement`. Verified empirically at the time: swapping in
kotva's signaling.ts + rendezvousSignaling.ts verbatim produced 10 tsc errors
in fabric.ts and call/fabricSignaling.ts (TS2345/TS2339/TS2353/TS2305/TS2322).
commit 091848c ("widen signaling.ts SignalPayload for real consumers") and
345be85 ("widen rendezvousSignaling.ts's signal() to match SignalKind") fixed
this UPSTREAM: `SignalKind` is now `SignalFrameType | (string & {})` (the five
core kinds still type-check; arbitrary app kinds are allowed), `toId` widened
to `string | null`, and `data?`/`identity?: unknown` added -- deliberately
excluded from the signed `_canonical` field set. Adopting verbatim now produces
3 tsc errors, both in pier's fabric.ts, both pier's own responsibility, not a
protocol gap: `SignedPreKeyAnnouncement` renamed to match upstream's
`SignedPreKeyClaim` (TS2305), and `_depositPubKeyB64: string | null` mapped to
`?? undefined` at its two `signal()` call sites since SignalData.pubKey is
`string | undefined` upstream, no null variant (TS2322). Both files are now
real .ts, byte-pinned like the rest, with no hand-written .d.ts sidecar.
This is an INTERIM mechanism, not the intended end state. The end state is an
ordinary version-pinned dependency on `kotva-client`. It is not one today for a
concrete, verified reason: npm has no subdirectory support for git dependencies
(npm 11.6.2 clones the repo and reads package.json at the CLONE ROOT, which for
kotva does not exist), so the Cargo tag-pin convention this repo uses for
kotva-core -- { git = "...kotva", tag = "core-v0.2.0" } -- has no npm equivalent.
See README.md 'Consuming kotva-client' for the one-line switch and what unblocks it.
A path dependency on a sibling ../kotva checkout was deliberately NOT used: this
repo already records what that costs, in crates/pier-cli/Cargo.toml, where the
kotva-depot path dep makes `cargo build` at the root require the sibling. The
hashes below make this gate self-contained instead -- it needs no kotva checkout
and no network, so it runs in CI exactly as it runs offline.
version_note: kotva-client's package.json version, unbumped -- NOT a precise pointer to this sync. `commit` is authoritative; see _comment PROVENANCE.
tag_note: last formally-cut bindings/js tag -- kotva is NOT tagged for this sync, `commit` below is past it and authoritative.
